cube: GlobalTravelEngine - Statistics Supplier Error API Hotel
label: Supplier API errors (hotels)
purpose: Number of hotel API requests the platform sent to suppliers, classified by outcome (correct, time-out, supplier error, not mapped, no results) and by detailed and raw supplier error codes. Used to monitor supplier reliability: error and time-out counts and rates by supplier, credential, customer and request type.
grain: Aggregated count of hotel API requests per day, supplier, credential, customer, request type and outcome/error code.
use_for: supplier api errors and error rates
requests by outcome (correct, time-out, supplier error, not mapped, no results)
most frequent detailed or raw supplier error codes
which suppliers, credentials, customers or request types cause the most failures
not_for: response times, results or response sizes of supplier requests (Statistics Supplier API Service, Statistics Hotel Supplier)
supplier connection locks (Supplier Lock API Hotel)
hotel locks in the booking flow (History Hotel Locks)

coverage.note: About one year of data, from October 2025 (that first month looks partial: 0.30 billion requests against 0.49 billion in November). Monthly volumes are 0.3 to 1.2 billion requests. Totals above 2,147,483,647 overflow in the cube, so quarters, years and all-time must be added up from months (see rules).

dates.label: Request date
dates.meaning: Day the request was sent to the supplier (the cube's only day-level date).

measures.name: [Requests]
measures.label: Supplier requests
measures.definition: Number of hotel API requests sent to suppliers, whatever the outcome. Filter by 'Error Types'[Error Type] to count time-outs, supplier errors, not-mapped requests, empty answers or correct responses.
measures.notes: Only measure of the cube. Error words need the named filter of the same name. Stored as a 32-bit integer: any total above 2,147,483,647 wraps to a wrong, often negative, number (the all-time total reads -335,023,693 instead of about 8.25 billion; the last 12 months read -743,745,675). Query by month or finer and add up in the app.

named_filters.name: timeouts
named_filters.meaning: Requests where the supplier did not answer in time (supplier timeouts).

named_filters.name: supplier errors
named_filters.meaning: Requests where the supplier returned an error (SUPPLIER GENERAL ERROR).

named_filters.name: not mapped
named_filters.meaning: Requests that failed because the hotel or room is not mapped for the supplier.

named_filters.name: no results
named_filters.meaning: Requests the supplier answered with no availability (a valid empty answer, not a failure).

named_filters.name: supplier api errors
named_filters.meaning: All failed requests: time-outs, supplier errors and not-mapped. Excludes 'No results' and 'Unknown' (see review).

named_filters.name: test customers
named_filters.meaning: Requests from customers in the testing market.

named_filters.name: requests via web-service administrators
named_filters.meaning: Requests that went through a third-party web-service administrator tool.

rules: [Requests] is a 32-bit integer in the cube: any total above 2,147,483,647 comes back wrapped (wrong, often negative). One month is safe (largest about 1.2 billion); quarters, years and all-time are not (Q1 2026 is about 2.4 billion). For periods longer than a month, query by month (or finer) and add up in the app. Never show a negative count.
Error, time-out and supplier-error rates = [Requests] with the outcome filter ÷ [Requests] without it, for the same period and breakdown. The cube has no rate measure.

Filter periods on 'Calendar'[Fecha]. Calendar column names are Spanish: Año = year, Trimestre = quarter, Mes = month, Semana = week, Día De La Semana = weekday, Cuatrimestre = four-month period. The *.Value date columns are period keys and fail when queried on their own.

These are outcomes of requests to suppliers. They are not supplier connection locks (Supplier Lock API Hotel: a lock rule blocked a supplier connection) and not hotel locks (History Hotel Locks: a hotel option failed for a customer in the booking flow).
Only request counts are stored here: no response times, results, bookings or money.
'Context'[Context] has the same value list as 'Request Types'[Request Type]; use Request Type.

review.question: Which outcomes count as "supplier API errors" (and in the error rate)?
options: Time Outs + SUPPLIER GENERAL ERROR + Not Mapped
Every outcome except Correct (also No results)
Time Outs + SUPPLIER GENERAL ERROR only
review.proposed: Time Outs + SUPPLIER GENERAL ERROR + Not Mapped
review.why: 'No results' is a valid answer (no availability), not a failure. 'Not Mapped' is a failed request even though the cause is mapping rather than the supplier.

review.question: Does plain "supplier errors" mean only the SUPPLIER GENERAL ERROR outcome, or every failed request?
options: All failed requests (the 'supplier api errors' filter)
review.why: It matches the stored category. Time-outs have their own word, and "supplier API errors" or "failed requests" covers all failures.
